sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Genesis**: Lord Birkenhead, Secretary of State for India, challenged Indians to produce a constitution acceptable to all communities.
• **Committee Composition**: Chaired by **Motilal Nehru**; included Sir Ali Imam, Tej Bahadur Sapru, M.S. Aney, Mangal Singh, Shuaib Qureshi, Subhash Chandra Bose, and G.R. Pradhan.
• **Core Objective**: To establish a **Dominion Status** framework as the immediate goal for India.
• **Key Metric**: The report was the first attempt to define 'Fundamental Rights' and secularism in an Indian constitutional context.

items.definition: A status where India would remain within the British Empire but possess full internal autonomy; rejected by the younger faction (Nehru/Bose).
A system where all voters cast ballots for a common candidate, regardless of religion; intended to foster national unity.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Linguistic Provinces**: Proposed creation of provinces based on linguistic lines.
• **Secular State**: No state religion; complete religious freedom.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Communal Friction**: Muslim League demanded 1/3rd representation in Central Legislature, which the report rejected.
• **Youth Dissent**: The 'Independence for India League' was formed by J.L. Nehru and S.C. Bose to oppose the Dominion Status goal.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'D-J-L-F' (Dominion, Joint, Linguistic, Fundamental).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Dominion Status (Goal), Joint Electorates (Method), Linguistic Provinces (Structure), Fundamental Rights (Content).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Nehru Report (1928) with the Nehru Committee (1923). The 1928 report explicitly rejected separate electorates, which is the most common point of confusion.

Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'The Nehru Report was the first indigenous attempt at constitutional engineering, reflecting the tension between liberal constitutionalism and radical nationalism.'

keyTakeaways: The Nehru Report was the first major Indian effort to draft a constitution.
It advocated for Dominion Status, which triggered the formation of the Independence for India League.
The rejection of separate electorates led to the permanent alienation of the Muslim League from the Congress.
